question: Explain why the emitter-base junction is forward biased and the collector-base junction is reverse biased when a transistor is used as an amplifier.

options.A: The emitter-base junction is forward biased to inject majority carriers from emitter into the base. The collector-base junction is reverse biased so its electric field collects most of these carriers. A small base-current change thereby controls a much larger collector-current change, enabling amplification.
options.B: Both emitter-base and collector-base junctions are reverse biased so no carriers are injected or collected.
options.C: The emitter-base junction is reverse biased to inject carriers, while collector-base is forward biased to block them.
options.D: Both junctions are forward biased only to make the transistor work as a resistor with no amplification.
